drafts.title: Front seats provide longer adjustable thigh support and rear passengers get class-competitive legroom
drafts.description: Customers (especially tall drivers) can extend front seat cushion length for full thigh support and rear passengers have legroom at least as good as main competitors so long-distance comfort is improved.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front seat cushion has an adjustable extension that increases effective thigh support by at least 80 mm measured from the standard cushion front; rear knee clearance (legroom) measured per OEM interior measurement procedure is >= 915 mm. Both measurements must be met in the standard vehicle configuration in the lab for 95% of tested seat positions.
assumptions: Typical class competitor rear knee clearance averages ~900 mm today; 915 mm provides a measurable advantage.
80 mm of additional cushion extension is a practical target to support occupants up to ~196 cm (6'5").
uncertainties: Interior packaging (battery, HVAC ducts) may constrain achievable cushion extension or rear-seat geometry.
Precise competitor legroom figures may vary regionally; final target may require benchmarking at time of development.

drafts.title: Seat memory reliably restores saved positions on first recall
drafts.description: When a customer selects a saved seating profile, the vehicle restores the saved seat position consistently so drivers do not need manual readjustment.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: On first recall, the seat returns to the saved position within ±20 mm linear and ±2° rotational of the saved values in 95% of trials across 20 different saved positions and occupant loading conditions.
assumptions: Measurement tolerances of ±20 mm and ±2° reflect perceptible fit and are achievable with today's seat actuators and sensors.
uncertainties: Variability from sensor calibration drift or battery voltage under extreme temperatures may affect restoration accuracy.

drafts.title: Cup holders fit common bottle sizes and retain bottles securely
drafts.description: Customers can place common beverage containers in the cup holders without wobble or spill risk during normal driving.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cup holders must securely accommodate bottles and cups up to 90 mm diameter (including common 1.0 L bottles) and retain them without excessive movement when subjected to a lateral acceleration of 0.2 g in a fixture test.
assumptions: Most common single-use and reusable beverage containers for the segment are ≤ 90 mm diameter.
uncertainties: Very large travel mugs or non-standard containers may still require adapters or aftermarket solutions.

drafts.title: Trunk includes an accessible 12 V socket able to run a typical portable cooler
drafts.description: Customers can plug a 12 V cooler into the trunk socket and run it without needing an adapter or the vehicle interior sockets.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A 12 V socket is installed in the trunk and can continuously supply at least 10 A (≈120 W) for one hour in a bench test while maintaining voltage within safe limits; the socket is usable without removing luggage and is protected by a fuse.
assumptions: Typical portable 12 V coolers draw up to ~8–10 A when compressor runs; 10 A continuous covers the majority of customer use-cases.
Trunk packaging allows a protected, accessible socket without compromising cargo space.
uncertainties: Some high-power coolers may exceed 10 A; customers with such coolers may still need an inverter or dedicated high-power outlet.

drafts.title: Ambient interior lighting offers notably more colors and finer brightness control
drafts.description: Customers can personalize interior ambient lighting with a wide color palette and fine brightness steps to match mood and visibility preferences.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Ambient lighting supports at least 64 distinct colors and a minimum of 10 brightness levels (including off), and customers can set at least two independent lighting zones (front and rear). Changes take effect within 1 second of selection in the UI.
assumptions: 64 colors and 10 brightness steps are perceived by customers as significantly more granular than current systems.
uncertainties: Hardware-led color reproduction tolerances may make some adjacent colors visually similar; UI must present meaningful presets.

drafts.title: Volume control provides precise, tactile, and drift-free adjustment
drafts.description: Customers can adjust audio volume with a physical control that feels precise, does not drift over time, and instantly changes system volume without needing screen interaction.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Physical volume adjustments result in audible volume change within 250 ms and maintain consistent step behavior over >10,000 actuations with no more than 1% failure rate (defined as an actuation that does not produce the expected volume change or tactile click).
assumptions: Customers equate 'reliable, non-drifting' control to consistent tactile feedback and predictable system response.
Maintenance of performance over 10,000 actuations reflects multi-year normal use.
uncertainties: Environmental extremes (extreme humidity, temperature) may affect tactile feel or electronic behavior; those should be addressed in durability testing.

drafts.title: Exterior access systems work reliably in winter (handles and hands-free tailgate)
drafts.description: Customers can open the vehicle and the trunk reliably in cold and icy conditions without multiple attempts or failure due to frozen handles or unresponsive hands-free operation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Flush door handles operate reliably (able to be opened by the user) after exposure to -25°C ambient with 10 mm ice accretion in 95% of lab trials; hands-free tailgate opens on the first valid gesture within 2.5 seconds in 95% of trials across 20 attempts per test condition (cold, wet, and with light luggage).
assumptions: A -25°C / 10 mm ice accretion test represents typical severe winter conditions in target markets.
Hands-free actuation can be tuned to footwear and gait differences to achieve the 95% first-attempt target.
uncertainties: Extreme ice thickness or mechanical freezing of seals may still require owner intervention (de-icing).
Achieving both reliable flush-handle operation and tight aerodynamic styling may require trade-offs in mechanism design.

drafts.title: Front-end meets new EU pedestrian protection rules (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers request that the vehicle front-end design complies with the new EU pedestrian protection regulation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope for customer-facing product requirements; refer to homologation and regulatory compliance processes for objective verification.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/homologation requirement requested by customers; compliance and specific test criteria belong to homologation scope, not a customer-facing feature draft.

drafts.title: Rear-seat airbags FMVSS 208 certification (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers request that rear-seat airbags obtain FMVSS 208 certification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope for customer-facing product requirements; certification is a regulatory/homologation activity and will be handled in compliance planning.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/certification request; homologation and certification belong to compliance scope, not a product requirement.

drafts.title: Headlights follow ECE R112 beam pattern rules in every market (regulatory request)
drafts.description: Customers request that headlights follow ECE R112 beam pattern rules across markets.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope for a customer-facing requirement; headlight beam compliance is part of homologation and market-specific approval processes.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/homologation request; compliance is handled by certification teams, not as a customer-facing product requirement.

drafts.title: Requested 12‑bit magnetic rotary encoder for volume knob (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers specifically asked that the volume knob uses a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope: this is an engineering/component specification rather than a customer-facing outcome; include in engineering spec backlog if needed.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific component/part request; engineering specification is out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Request for 4.5 mm laminated side windows (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the side windows use 4.5 mm thick laminated glass.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope as a customer-facing requirement; this is a specific material/thickness engineering demand to be assessed in glazing and NVH engineering.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific technical/material specification requested by customers; glazing thickness is an engineering decision and thus out of scope.

drafts.title: Requested seat cushion foam density of 55 kg/m³ (engineering specification)
drafts.description: Customers asked for seat cushions specified with foam density of 55 kg per cubic meter.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope as a direct customer-facing requirement; foam density is a material specification for seat engineering and durability testing.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific material/component specification; engineering-level detail that belongs in technical specification documents.

drafts.title: Request for BMW to guarantee 60% residual value after 5 years (financial request)
drafts.description: Customers requested that BMW guarantees a residual value of 60% after five years.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope for product requirements (price/financial guarantees are a commercial/business decision).
drafts.scope_reason: Financial guarantee / price-related request; out of scope for engineering/product requirement drafts.

drafts.title: Request to cut production cost per car by 8% (business request)
drafts.description: Customers (or internal feedback) asked for BMW to cut production cost per car by 8 percent.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Out of scope: production cost targets are a business/operations objective, not a customer-facing feature requirement.
drafts.scope_reason: Production cost targets are a business/operational objective and not a customer-facing product requirement.
